lastPrompt: You are given: A MonoGame source tree at /workspace/MonoGame A deterministic headless mini-game project at /workspace/game_project (Transform Arena) Replay and expected-output assets under /workspace/assets Your task is to complete a full bootstrap workflow: Phase A - Engine and game repair, then verification 1) Complete intentionally hollowed Microsoft XNA Framework 3D transform math (Vector3 and Matrix public API surface used by the replay). The task contains large missing implementations. The existing code around the hollowed sections may also have potential correctness issues. You must retrieve code context across modules and restore correct behavior end-to-end. 2) Complete the game-side C# project under /workspace/game_project (replay runner, replay I/O, simulation world). Together they are on the order of several hundred lines. The game is a partial skeleton with an intentional seed mismatch in the replay runner; final behavior must be deterministic and driven by Vector3 and Matrix operations, not hard-coded end states. 3) Build the MonoGame DesktopGL framework and test host, then run a selected set of MonoGame framework unit tests and save a machine-readable report. Phase B - Game replay verification 4) Run the headless mini-game replay twice using the same seed and replay input. The game must exercise 3D vector math, matrix-vector transforms, 3D distance queries, and Point-to-Vector2 conversion on the same call chain as the hollowed engine code. 5) Export final state JSON and its SHA256 hash for each run. 6) Confirm replay determinism (two same-seed runs produce identical state hash). Phase C - Integrated acceptance 7) Produce all required output artifacts listed below. 8) Ensure outputs match expected integrity checks. Required output files: /workspace/output/engine_checks.json /workspace/output/engine_test_stdout.log /[redacted].json /[redacted].sha256 /[redacted].jsonl /[redacted].json /[redacted].json /[redacted].sha256 /[redacted].jsonl /[redacted].json /workspace/output/game_final_state.json /workspace/output/game_final_state.sha256 /workspace/output/determinism_report.json Rules: Automated grading (pytest) checks engine_checks.json, math event types, engine trace flags, replay determinism, and compares the run SHA256 to a reference value stored only under /tests (not in the agent workspace). Do not edit files under /tests. Do not bypass replay execution. Do not fabricate hashes; compute them from the actual JSON outputs you generate. The final hash must be computed from canonicalized JSON content. Do not replace vector- and matrix-driven simulation with manual state mutation. Do not edit files under /workspace/game_project/tests (if present). Do not bypass engine-side missing implementations by stubbing outputs. Engine fixes must be made on the 3D math types used by the game. You are running as a long-horizon autonomous engineering agent at `/workspace`. This task spans many files and requirements, and is expected to take many iterations. Read every requirement under `/workspace/requirements/` (and any other explicit requirement list referenced by the task) and only finish once every single one is addressed. Cherry-picking or partial fixes will lead to failure. ## Optional planning artifact If you believe the task is complex enough to benefit from a plan, you may write `/workspace/agent_plans/plan.json` before making changes. This is optional. If you create it, it must be a JSON object with `nodes` and `edges`. Each node must have string `id` equal to a requirement slug from `/workspace/requirements/`, may include `label` and `layer`, and each edge must use string `from` and `to` that reference those ids. ## Git workflow (required) `/workspace` is initialized as a git repo.
